children: Singapore Exchange faces pressure on earnings as moderating growth in derivatives and securities fails to justify the stock's premium valuation, Macquarie Equity Research analyst Jayden Vantarakis says in a note. Derivatives growth is normalizing from a high three-year base, the analyst says. Meanwhile, securities average daily value needs to rise to 2.9 billion Singapore dollars-S$3.5 billion to justify where the stock is trading, compared with the S$2.0 billion-S$2.2 billion range currently. Macquarie trims its 2027-2029 EPS estimates by 2% and downgrades the stock to underperform from neutral, citing a 30% premium to Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing. It also cuts its target price by 22% to S$20.30. Shares are down 4.1% at S$23.30. (venkat.pr@wsj.com)
